mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS against 20-day forward returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not negative (Pearson correlation < -0.1) in the most recent 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market tightness indicator (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals high unemployment, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5%, or the average 20-day return in high UNRATE periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust economic activity across supply and demand sectors, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when both INDPRO and HOUST are above their 3-month moving averages is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05), or the interaction term in a regression of 20-day returns on INDPRO and HOUST (with interaction) is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals higher borrowing costs that reduce corporate investment and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return during periods when FEDFUNDS is rising and the regime is monetary tightening is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS (in tightening cycles) is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market boom (HOUST > 2200 thousand units) signals strong consumer confidence and increased construction activity, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 2200, or the average 20-day return in high HOUST periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery phase (as indicated by a sustained increase in payroll employment), a strong labor market supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return during periods when PAYEMS is rising and the regime is labor market recovery is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for PAYEMS (in recovery regimes) is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO against 5-day forward returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between INDPRO and 5-day returns is not positive (Pearson correlation < 0.1) in the most recent 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of retail sales (RSAFS > 330,000 million dollars) signals strong consumer spending, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 330000, or the average 60-day return in high RSAFS periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
